Remember the definition of repression you learned earlier? Sometimes repression isn't enough of a defense. When this is the case a person adds additional defenses, behaving exactly the opposite to the way that he/she wants to behave. Such a defense is called reaction formation.�

Reaction formation can be distinguished for its flagrance, exaggeration and compulsiveness.�

For example, although John is actually a very shy and dependent individual, he becomes a loud and demanding executive in charge of a large and successful company.

Another example: A mother who resents the many demands of her children may become over-protective of them; she is acting in the opposite way to her true feelings.�

Further example: Tommy is a shy fifteen year old. He really likes Maria but ignores her and acts gruff in her presence to hide his true feelings.
